create.title: One-factor functional-equation reduction of the diagonal transition traces
create.statement_tex: Factor the centered degree-two completion into the completed zeta factor at s+z/2 and completed chi_4 factor at s-z/2. On the beta-bounded trace, undo the low-height zeta functional equation and retain only the high-height chi_4 functional equation; on the alpha-bounded trace, undo the low-height chi_4 functional equation and retain only the high-height zeta functional equation. Derive exact finite mixed-chamber formulas, including moving poles, axial/top residues, outside segments, actual profiles, and normalization, then prove a target-sized bound or a rigorous obstruction.
create.next_action: Derive both exact mixed-factor trace formulas and test whether the chi_4-high branch admits character Abel while the zeta-high branch requires pole-subtracted eta/Euler-Maclaurin cancellation.

update.next_action: Test the one-factor functional-equation mixed-chamber reduction for both diagonal traces, with the closed endpoint/residue package removed exactly once.
Resolve the two diagonal traces through the partial-functional-equation reduction; all radial endpoint/residue terms are already target-safe.

no_change.reason: The proposed mixed-factor reduction is not yet proved or estimated.
The transition traces and residual direct corridor remain open.

round_assessment.reason: Round-24 closure isolates the pair of transition traces and records a factor-by-factor functional-equation strategy without claiming that it succeeds.
